artifacts.summary: Design research for a durable, cross-invocation redeploy ledger (content hash + recency/attribution skip) for the /orchestrate inter-cycle redeploy checkpoint, including a correction of the dispatch's guardrails-doc citation and two concrete design options (extend .claude-extensions.json vs. a new gitignored durable ledger file).

next_steps: Run /plan 182 to create an implementation plan

memory_candidates.content: The repo already has a durable, git-tracked, tested content-hash-freshness mechanism at scripts/lib/deploy-freshness-lib.sh (deploy_freshness_status), keyed against .claude-extensions.json's per-extension source_git_head field. Before building a new durable content-hash ledger for orchestrator source-store state, check whether this existing mechanism can be reused or extended rather than duplicated -- it already answers 'has agent-system/extensions/<ext> changed since the last recorded deploy' with a fail-safe CANNOTVERIFY/STALE/FRESH three-way result.

In context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md, the guardrails doc has two sibling ### sections both discussing deployed_critical_paths: 'The Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint' (its own idempotence guard, within-invocation) and 'The Postflight Completion-Deploy Gate' (a residual D6 note about widening the trigger predicate, which also mentions deployed_critical_paths and says widening it 'is its own task'). These are easy to conflate when a task description points at 'the deployed_critical_paths idempotence backing store... its own task' quote -- verify which section a quote actually lives in before assuming it names the current task's scope.
